_comment: The realm shell.online signs in against. Imported on first start only:
Keycloak skips a realm that already exists rather than overwriting it, so
changes made in the admin console survive restarts and this file is the
starting point rather than the running truth.
registrationAllowed is false: this deployment is a handful of people, and
a realm on the public internet that lets anyone register is a realm that
will have strangers in it. Accounts are created in the admin console.
Turning it on makes Keycloak show a Register link on its own sign-in page;
the app needs no change for that.
The client is public and PKCE-only. A browser cannot keep a secret, so
there is none to keep: the proof key is what binds the authorization code
to the browser that asked for it. S256 is required rather than offered,
because a client that may fall back to `plain` gains nothing from PKCE.
